rv.q: It is with a heavy heart that I have to report that this calculated, potentially refreshing gamble has not paid off in a production by Anna Mackmin that is damagingly deficient in tension or any sense of sick, black-joke inexorability as the escape hatches close on a heroine whose schemes all backfire.
Sheridan Smith makes for one hell of a bitch.
While this may not be the best Hedda Gabler that you could ever see, it effortlessly holds the attention for three hours, mainly through comedy.
But in this richly intelligent performance, Smith conveys Hedda’s material ambition, her boredom and her deluded romantic idealism.
